example: A Cargo and mdBook project that lists `habeas` only under `[dependencies]` gets no session-start agent context, neither the skill sentence nor a setup advisory. {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.not_applicable`
rationale:
The example is covered by `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_gives_no_context_outside_habeas_projects]`, which carries a {test} reference to `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.runtime_dependency_only`.

**Setup.** `fixture()` builds a Cargo project (`Cargo.toml`, `src/main.rs`) that is also an mdBook project (`book.toml`, `md/SUMMARY.md`). The test appends `[dependencies]\nhabeas = "0.2"` to the manifest. That matches the scenario: both project kinds, with `habeas` listed only under `[dependencies]`. The same loop also covers `[build-dependencies]`.

**Run.** `session_start()` runs the real `habeas hook session-start` binary. It passes a SessionStart JSON on stdin with `cwd` set to the project, and it asserts the process succeeded.

**Assertion.** The test asserts the output equals `{"SessionStart": {}}`. That output contains no context at all, so it has neither the skill sentence nor a setup advisory. The example states both outcomes, and this single equality covers both.

The test also checks the neighbouring cases of the cited requirement: a directory outside any project, a project that doesn't list `habeas`, and a dev-dependency without mdBook.

text: A Cargo and mdBook project that lists `habeas` only under `[dependencies]` gets no session-start agent context, neither the skill sentence nor a setup advisory. {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.not_applicable`
When a session starts outside every Cargo and mdBook project, or within one whose manifest does not list `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, the hook MUST provide no agent context.
